rules.text: 1.14. When you must draw a card from an empty deck (i.e. there are 0 cards in your deck area), you lose immediately.

rules.title: If you attempt to draw more cards than remain in your deck, the first card you cannot draw counts as drawing from an…
rules.text:
1.14.1. If you attempt to draw more cards than remain in your deck, the first card you cannot draw counts as drawing from an empty deck. See Draw.

> **EXAMPLE:** A card effect says “Draw 2,” but you only have 1 card left in your deck area. You draw the first card, and attempt to draw the second card. The deck is now empty, so you lose immediately.

rules.title: A game value can be a negative number.
rules.text: 2.10. A game value can be a negative number.

rules.title: When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
rules.text:
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit has 2 power. An effect reduces its power by 3. The Unit has -1 power, but is treated as having 0 power when attacking, fighting, or when a card effect references its power. If it then gains +2 power, that Unit has 1 power. The order of these effects being applied does not alter this outcome.

rules.title: A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number.
rules.text: 2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

rules.text: 5.9.3. Cards in this area are placed face-up in a pile, and either player can freely view the contents and order of these cards.

rules.title: When placing new cards in this area, they are placed on top of the previous card already in the pile.
rules.text: 5.9.4. When placing new cards in this area, they are placed on top of the previous card already in the pile.

rules.title: If multiple cards enter this area at the same time, their owner adds them in any order.
rules.text: 5.9.4.1. If multiple cards enter this area at the same time, their owner adds them in any order.

rules.title: Players may freely change the order of cards in their own trash.
rules.text: 5.9.4.2. Players may freely change the order of cards in their own trash. The cards in the trash should always remain in the face-up position unless specified otherwise.

rules.title: If a card effect triggers when a Gig would be stolen, resolve the effect after the Gig is selected, but before the Gi…
rules.text:
6.7.4. If a card effect triggers when a Gig would be stolen, resolve the effect after the Gig is selected, but before the Gig changes control.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit’s card text reads “When a rival Unit would steal a Gig, you may discard 1 with cost equal to that Gig's value. If you do, the Gig isn't stolen.” A rival Unit attacks your Gig area to steal 2 Gigs. Your Rival chooses to steal Gigs with values 3 and 10. You discard a card with cost 3, so the rival Unit only steals the value 10 Gig.

rules.title: An effect is card text that affects the game.
rules.text: 10.1. An effect is card text that affects the game. Card text is the source of effects.

rules.title: Within card text, a line break indicates the end of the effect text.
rules.text: 10.1.1. Within card text, a line break indicates the end of the effect text.

rules.title: Each separate paragraph on a card is considered a single effect.
rules.text: 10.1.2. Each separate paragraph on a card is considered a single effect.

rules.title: When an effect refers to “this card,” “this Unit,” “this Legend,” “this Gear,” or another similar phrase, it refers t…
rules.text: 10.1.3. When an effect refers to “this card,” “this Unit,” “this Legend,” “this Gear,” or another similar phrase, it refers to the source of that effect unless another rule or effect says otherwise.

rules.title: If you control the source of an effect, it is considered “your” effect.
rules.text: 10.1.4. If you control the source of an effect, it is considered “your” effect. You are the one who resolves it.

rules.title: To “resolve” an effect, follow the instructions of that effect in the order they appear.
rules.text: 10.2. To “resolve” an effect, follow the instructions of that effect in the order they appear.

rules.title: Always resolve as much of an effect as possible.
rules.text: 10.2.1. Always resolve as much of an effect as possible. See GOLDEN RULES > Resolve as Much as Possible.

rules.title: If an effect instructs both players to act at the same time, the turn player performs their actions first, followed b…
rules.text: 10.2.2. If an effect instructs both players to act at the same time, the turn player performs their actions first, followed by their Rival.

rules.title: Once an effect starts resolving, you cannot play cards, activate effects, or resolve other pending effects until the…
rules.text: 10.2.3. Once an effect starts resolving, you cannot play cards, activate effects, or resolve other pending effects until the current effect finishes resolving.

rules.title: Effects cannot interrupt the activation or resolution of other effects.
rules.text: 10.2.4. Effects cannot interrupt the activation or resolution of other effects. If an effect triggers in the middle of an activation or resolution, it becomes “pending resolution.” See EFFECTS > Pending Resolution.

rules.title: After an effect resolves, perform any required rule processing before resolving a new one or taking any actions.
rules.text: 10.2.5. After an effect resolves, perform any required rule processing before resolving a new one or taking any actions.

rules.title: An effect may include conditions.
rules.text: 10.3. An effect may include conditions. A “condition” is a requirement that must be true for an effect to apply, become pending, and resolve. (Conditions are often “if” or “when” clauses.)

rules.title: If a condition is false, do not apply its corresponding effect.
rules.text: 10.3.1. If a condition is false, do not apply its corresponding effect.

rules.title: A condition is not a cost unless it is specifically within a cost.
rules.text: 10.3.2. A condition is not a cost unless it is specifically within a cost. See Cost.

rules.title: A condition within an effect’s resolution is checked when that part of the effect resolves.
rules.text: 10.3.3. A condition within an effect’s resolution is checked when that part of the effect resolves.

rules.title: If an effect requires a target or choice with no legal options, the effect is invalid and the controlling player does…
rules.text: 10.7. If an effect requires a target or choice with no legal options, the effect is invalid and the controlling player does not make a choice.

rules.title: If an effect instructs a player to choose, select, or otherwise make a choice, that choice is made when the effect in…
rules.text: 10.31. If an effect instructs a player to choose, select, or otherwise make a choice, that choice is made when the effect instructs the player to make that choice.

rules.title: If an effect requires a choice and no legal choice can be made, that choice is not made.
rules.text: 10.31.1. If an effect requires a choice and no legal choice can be made, that choice is not made.

rules.title: If an effect requires you to choose a specific number of targets, you must choose that number of targets.
rules.text: 10.31.2. If an effect requires you to choose a specific number of targets, you must choose that number of targets. If you can’t, choose as many valid targets as possible up to that number instead.

rules.title: If an effect requires a player to choose a number, that player must choose a non-negative whole number.
rules.text: 10.31.3. If an effect requires a player to choose a number, that player must choose a non-negative whole number.

rules.title: If multiple choices are required while resolving an effect, make those choices in the order written.
rules.text: 10.32. If multiple choices are required while resolving an effect, make those choices in the order written.

rules.text: 11.2.1. Your “Street Cred” is the sum of all Gig dice values in the friendly Gig area.

rules.title: Draw
“Draw” is a game action in which you move the top card of your deck to your hand.
rules.text: 11.5.1. “Draw” is a game action in which you move the top card of your deck to your hand.

rules.title: When an effect says “Draw X” (where X is a number), take the draw action X number of times.
rules.text: 11.5.2. When an effect says “Draw X” (where X is a number), take the draw action X number of times. Literally, it means “move the top card of your deck to your hand, X individual times.”

rules.title: When you “Draw X,” draw each card individually.
rules.text: 11.5.2.1. When you “Draw X,” draw each card individually. Do not take multiple cards from the top of your deck at once.

rules.title: When you “Draw up to X,” choose the number of cards you will draw, then draw exactly that number of cards.
rules.text: 11.5.2.2. When you “Draw up to X,” choose the number of cards you will draw, then draw exactly that number of cards.

rules.title: If you attempt to draw more cards than remain in your deck, it counts as drawing from an empty deck.
rules.text: 11.5.2.3. If you attempt to draw more cards than remain in your deck, it counts as drawing from an empty deck. See GAME OVERVIEW > Lose Conditions.

decisions.shape: Complete Blue RAM3 Doll Unit; cost2 power0 no Sell tag. Printed ATTACK is one ordered ability: DRAW1 then conditional controller-chosen own-hand DISCARD1. Zero-power stealing reminder uses existing current-power rules; it is not a permanent cannot-steal restriction.
decisions.sequence: 10.2/10.2.3/10.3.3: DRAW updates authoritative state before the second clause is evaluated. No other pending effect, Quick, CALL or Blocker interleaves. DRAW does not change derived Street Cred.
decisions.condition: 11.2/5.11.4/2.10: current sum of friendly Gig values greater than rival. Numeric beats Null, equal numeric and Null/Null are false. No stored counter or trigger-time snapshot.
decisions.chooser: 10.1.4 effect source controller resolves its mandatory instruction; 10.31 choices at resolution. The printed you applies to draw and discard; rival appears only in the comparison. No may, random, opponent selection or rival-hand access permission is printed.
decisions.discard: Local comprehensive snapshot has no standalone DISCARD glossary entry. Reviewed synthesis: ordinary discard is an own-hand selection (corroborated by captured Shattered Memories discard their hand wording), 10.1.4/10.31 assign the choice to the resolving player, and the official Gameplay Guide Trash definition explicitly places discarded cards face-up in Trash. Do not generalize to another player choosing, random discard, other origin areas or cross-owner cards.
decisions.shortfall: 10.31.1/10.31.2 resolve as much as possible: zero eligible cards creates no choice, one mandatory card resolves automatically, multiple legal cards create DISCARD_SELECTION. For Evelyn specifically, successful DRAW1 guarantees at least one own-hand card; empty-deck loss under1.14 stops before the condition.
decisions.visibility: 5.4 own hand visible only to its player, rival sees count. 5.9 Trash public and ordered; discarded identity becomes public after movement. Authoritative events are private replay records, not model input.
decisions.continuation: Existing ATTACK trigger binding pins source revision, subject/controller, turn/batch and return origin. Optional primitiveIndex=1 identifies second clause; conditionMet=true records evaluated gate. No admitted interleaving can change Gigs while paused.
decisions.knowledge: Discard only moves a hand card. Existing friendly Legend memories and public known markers remain untouched.
